protocol_deviations: CALL remains synchronous: the caller waits for the child's terminal return, and 'represent waiting parents separately from actively consuming worker slots' (issue text) is deferred to the concurrency waves — the issue itself marks concurrency as coming from parallel scopes, not from CALL.

The issue's proposed `CALL protocol.name AS child(...)` syntax was intentionally not implemented; the sealed program and runtime use the current standalone `CALL protocol.name(args) -> targets` grammar, so parser.py is untouched this wave.

CHILD_ADOPTED's adopted payload maps target -> child ref (as specified in the implementation guidance); the adopted VALUES travel only inside the CALL's SUCCEEDED delta, so the event alone is evidence, not state.

The parent's invocation-id sequence no longer continues across the CALL boundary (pre-#20 inline behavior); the child owns inv-1..inv-N in its own namespace. Task texts also change from 'protocol.name: step.x: DO cmd' to a single 'CALL protocol.name' entry in the parent plus unprefixed texts in the child. The external driver (envelope.py) is unaffected because it rejects CALL programs up front.

A protocol that RETURNs a ref it RETIREd (or a declared INPUT that no step ever targeted and that is not returned via the seeded binding) is non-adoptable: adoption reads the child's committed state (seeded INPUT bindings plus replayed deltas), so the parent fails with 'did not commit RETURN reference <ref>' instead of publishing a phantom. Declared-INPUT pass-through RETURNs ARE adoptable.

resume_run's deferred windows from #10 remain (W5 result adoption without a worker re-call; W3 external idempotency query). Child-side equivalents follow the same at-least-once contract: a non-terminal child's in-flight worker call is re-executed on resume, deduplicated by the child's own run:invocation idempotency keys.

The demo program's stub-worker end-to-end verification used deterministic handlers for the 22 registered commands executed directly through SequentialCoordinator; the model-backed worker path (worker_adapter.py, untouched this wave) is exercised by its own existing tests.
